cleanIntro: The 2K11 strips without a bushing wrench and without a paperclip: the guide rod is tool-less, and the whole job turns on unloading its spring FIRST. Do that before the slide stop moves and nothing is fighting you; do it after and the spring is what launches across the room.

steps.title: Unloaded, locked back, eyes protected
steps.action: Muzzle safe, fingers outside the guard, unload it and lock the slide back, then LOOK at the magazine well and the chamber. Kimber asks for eye protection through the whole strip, and the reason is two paragraphs further down the page.
steps.aside: Exercise great caution as the recoil spring and plug are under tension and can fly out with enough force to cause serious injury or property damage.
steps.quote: Lock the slide back and visually inspect the magazine well and chamber are empty.
steps.cite: Kimber 2K11 Pistol Models Safety & Instruction Manual — Safety & Instruction Manual. ⛔ No part, form or revision code and no copyright year is printed anywhere in this book — the same gap every Kimber manual in the drop has. — Disassembly (Field Stripping) & Assembly

steps.title: ⛔ Tool-less guide rod: push IN, rotate COUNTER-clockwise
steps.action: Push in on the front of the tool-less guide rod and rotate it counter-clockwise. That takes the tension off the recoil spring and it is the first step for a reason — everything after it is a part being lifted out rather than a spring being restrained.
steps.quote: Push in on the front of the tool-less guide rod and rotate counterclockwise to remove the tension from the recoil spring.
steps.cite: Kimber 2K11 Pistol Models Safety & Instruction Manual — Safety & Instruction Manual. ⛔ No part, form or revision code and no copyright year is printed anywhere in this book — the same gap every Kimber manual in the drop has. — Disassembly (Field Stripping) & Assembly

steps.title: Slide stop out through the notch
steps.action: Line the slide stop up with the notch on the slide, then push on the leg on the OPPOSITE side of the pistol to start it out. Pushing from the same side you are pulling is why people mark their frames.
steps.quote: Align the slide stop with the notch on the slide and remove the slide stop pushing on the leg on the opposite side of the firearm.
steps.cite: Kimber 2K11 Pistol Models Safety & Instruction Manual — Safety & Instruction Manual. ⛔ No part, form or revision code and no copyright year is printed anywhere in this book — the same gap every Kimber manual in the drop has. — Disassembly (Field Stripping) & Assembly

steps.title: Slide forward off the subframe, then rod and barrel
steps.action: Run the slide forward off the SUBFRAME — the 2K11's serialised part is the subframe, not the grip — then lift out the tool-less guide rod assembly and the barrel. That is the strip; Kimber says outright that nothing further is needed for general cleaning.
steps.aside: The firearm is now disassembled. No further disassembly is required for general cleaning.
steps.quote: Remove the slide from the subframe by pushing the slide forward.
steps.cite: Kimber 2K11 Pistol Models Safety & Instruction Manual — Safety & Instruction Manual. ⛔ No part, form or revision code and no copyright year is printed anywhere in this book — the same gap every Kimber manual in the drop has. — Disassembly (Field Stripping) & Assembly

steps.title: ⛔ Slide off means the hammer stays where it is
steps.action: With the slide off the subframe, do not drop the hammer and do not dry fire. Kimber prints both, separately, on this pistol — dry firing it in that condition can damage the gun.
steps.aside: Do not dry fire your Kimber 2K11 pistol while the slide is removed. Doing so can cause damage to the firearm.
steps.quote: Do not drop the hammer while the slide is removed from the pistol.
steps.cite: Kimber 2K11 Pistol Models Safety & Instruction Manual — Safety & Instruction Manual. ⛔ No part, form or revision code and no copyright year is printed anywhere in this book — the same gap every Kimber manual in the drop has. — Disassembly (Field Stripping) & Assembly

steps.title: ⛔ Rod in from the CHAMBER end, every time
steps.action: The cleaning rod enters at the chamber, never the muzzle. Wet patch with bore solvent, let it soak a few minutes, dry patch to lift the loose debris — and read the solvent maker's own directions, because some of them will lift a finish as happily as they lift fouling.
steps.aside: Run a patch wet with bore cleaning solvent through the barrel bore and let the solution soak a few minutes.
steps.quote: Always insert a cleaning rod from the chamber end of the barrel.
steps.cite: Kimber 2K11 Pistol Models Safety & Instruction Manual — Safety & Instruction Manual. ⛔ No part, form or revision code and no copyright year is printed anywhere in this book — the same gap every Kimber manual in the drop has. — CLEANING

steps.title: Wet brush through and OUT the muzzle, then repeat to clean
steps.action: Push the wet bore brush in at the chamber and all the way OUT of the muzzle before drawing it back — reversing a brush inside the bore folds the bristles over. Dry patch after, and repeat the pair until a patch comes out clean. Then a light oil, and ⛔ a dry patch through before you ever fire it.
steps.aside: Run a dry patch through the barrel before firing to remove oil.
steps.quote: Run a wet bore brush through the chamber end of the barrel and out the muzzle,making several passes.
steps.cite: Kimber 2K11 Pistol Models Safety & Instruction Manual — Safety & Instruction Manual. ⛔ No part, form or revision code and no copyright year is printed anywhere in this book — the same gap every Kimber manual in the drop has. — CLEANING

steps.title: Breech face and every bearing surface — nylon brush
steps.action: Wipe the dirt off all the bearing surfaces on the slide and frame, then get into the breech face and the rest of the parts with a toothbrush or similar nylon brush. ⛔ And no ultrasonic tank: Kimber says damage from one is not covered by warranty, and night sights must never go near it.
steps.aside: Do not expose night sights to an ultrasonic cleaning environment.
steps.quote: Clean the breech face and all parts (a toothbrush or similar nylon brush works well).
steps.cite: Kimber 2K11 Pistol Models Safety & Instruction Manual — Safety & Instruction Manual. ⛔ No part, form or revision code and no copyright year is printed anywhere in this book — the same gap every Kimber manual in the drop has. — CLEANING

steps.title: Lubricate by the drop, at the points Kimber names
steps.action: Premium oil, not grease — and if it carries Teflon, shake it, because the Teflon settles overnight and you will otherwise apply the carrier and none of the additive. Then oil only where this book says, in the quantities it gives.
steps.aside: Barrel locking lugs inside slide and on barrel; 1 drop on each lug.
steps.quote: Slide and subframe rails; 3 drops on each side.
steps.cite: Kimber 2K11 Pistol Models Safety & Instruction Manual — Safety & Instruction Manual. ⛔ No part, form or revision code and no copyright year is printed anywhere in this book — the same gap every Kimber manual in the drop has. — LUBRICATION

steps.title: ⛔ Nothing in the firing pin channel, and wipe the excess
steps.action: Reassemble, work the slide five or six times, dry fire, then wipe off the excess. Moderation is the whole point: too little and it wears, too much and it collects the grit that wears it faster. ⛔ And if it has been stored oiled, a dry patch goes through the barrel before firing.
steps.quote: If the firearm has been stored with oil in the barrel and chamber, push a dry patch through the barrel before firing.
steps.cite: Kimber 2K11 Pistol Models Safety & Instruction Manual — Safety & Instruction Manual. ⛔ No part, form or revision code and no copyright year is printed anywhere in this book — the same gap every Kimber manual in the drop has. — LUBRICATION

deepAbsentReason: Kimber's limit is printed in the strip itself — "The firearm is now disassembled. No further disassembly is required for general cleaning." — and again as a warning: "Do not disassemble your firearm beyond field stripping outlined in this manual. Do not manipulate any internal components beyond what you are instructed to do in this manual." Going further voids the warranty in Kimber's own words. A manufacturer's published DON'T outranks every other tier, so nothing deeper is authored from anywhere else.

cleaning.name: BARREL
tasks: ⛔ Rod ALWAYS from the chamber end
Wet patch, soak a few minutes, dry patch
Wet brush in at the chamber and OUT the muzzle before drawing back
Repeat until a patch comes out clean, then a light oil

cleaning.name: SLIDE & FRAME
tasks: Breech face and parts with a nylon brush
⛔ No ultrasonic cleaning — the damage is not warranted

cleaning.name: LUBRICATION
tasks: Premium oil, NOT grease; shake it if it contains Teflon
Only the points this model's book names, in the drops it gives
⛔ Never into the firing pin channel
Work the slide 5-6 times, dry fire, wipe the excess off

cleaning.name: MAGAZINES
tasks: Wiped clean; follower checked to slide freely

reassembly: Slide upside down in one hand; barrel in from the MUZZLE end with its link forward, clear of the recoil spring tunnel.
Tool-less guide rod in from the BREECH end, contoured edge of the head toward the barrel and the radius edge outward.
Slide onto the subframe rails and run back until the slide stop notch lines up.
Slide stop in, then the guide rod pushed in and rotated back to load the spring.
Cycle the slide several times, dry fire, wipe off excess lubrication.
fncheck: Reassembled and unloaded: work the slide five or six times, confirm it returns fully into battery, and check the tool-less guide rod is rotated back into its locked position before you trust it. Dry fire once, wipe the excess oil off, and function check the safety.
